source_text:
AFTER VISIT SUMMARY
Sample Patient   DOB: 01/01/1970   Visit: 10/01/2026   Midtown Family Medicine (sample clinic)
Provider: Sample Provider, MD

Reason for visit: Follow-up for high blood sugar and blood pressure.

Your diagnoses today:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications (E11.9)
- Essential hypertension (I10)

Medication changes
START taking these medications:
- metformin (GLUCOPHAGE) 500 mg tablet. Take 1 tablet by mouth 2 times a day with meals.
CHANGE how you take these medications:
- lisinopril 10 mg tablet. Take 2 tablets (20 mg total) by mouth once daily. Previously 10 mg once daily.
STOP taking these medications:
- ibuprofen (ADVIL) 200 mg tablet. Avoid NSAIDs due to kidney function.

Orders placed today
- Hemoglobin A1c - due in 3 months
- Basic metabolic panel - fasting, complete within 2 weeks at any Quest or Labcorp location
- Referral to Ophthalmology for diabetic eye exam. Their office will call you to schedule. If you have not heard from them in 10 days, call 404-555-0134.

Follow-up
Return to clinic in 3 months, or sooner if needed.

Patient instructions
Check your blood sugar every morning before breakfast and write down the number. Bring your log to your next visit.
Walk 30 minutes, 5 days a week, as tolerated.
Limit sugary drinks such as soda and sweet tea.

When to seek care
Call the office if your blood sugar is above 300 two times in a row.
Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room if you have chest pain, trouble breathing, or sudden weakness on one side of your body.

items.title: Start metformin
items.plain_language: This is a new medicine. Take 1 pill (500 mg) two times a day. Take it with food.
items.why: It helps lower your blood sugar. You have type 2 diabetes.
items.when: 2 times a day with meals, starting now
items.source_quote: metformin (GLUCOPHAGE) 500 mg tablet. Take 1 tablet by mouth 2 times a day with meals.

items.title: Take more lisinopril
items.plain_language: Your dose went up. Now take 2 pills (20 mg total) one time each day. Before, you took 1 pill (10 mg).
items.why: It is for your high blood pressure.
items.source_quote: lisinopril 10 mg tablet. Take 2 tablets (20 mg total) by mouth once daily. Previously 10 mg once daily.

items.title: Stop ibuprofen (Advil)
items.plain_language: Do not take ibuprofen (Advil) anymore. Stay away from this type of pain medicine (called NSAIDs).
items.why: The paper says it is because of how your kidneys are working.
items.source_quote: ibuprofen (ADVIL) 200 mg tablet. Avoid NSAIDs due to kidney function.
items.question_for_clinic: What can I safely take for pain instead, and which medicines count as NSAIDs?

items.title: A1c blood test
items.plain_language: This is a blood test. You need it in about 3 months.
items.why: It shows your average blood sugar over the last few months.
items.question_for_clinic: Where should I get my A1c test done, and do I need an appointment?

items.title: Basic metabolic panel blood test
items.plain_language: This is a blood test. Do not eat before it (fasting). Go to any Quest or Labcorp lab.
items.why: The paper does not say why. It is a blood test ordered at your visit.
items.source_quote: Basic metabolic panel - fasting, complete within 2 weeks at any Quest or Labcorp location
items.question_for_clinic: How many hours should I go without food before this test? Can I drink water or take my medicines that morning?

items.title: Eye doctor visit
items.plain_language: You will see an eye doctor for a diabetes eye check. Their office will call you to set it up. If they do not call in 10 days, call 404-555-0134.
items.why: It is a diabetes eye exam.
items.when: Wait for their call. Call them if you hear nothing in 10 days.
items.source_quote: Referral to Ophthalmology for diabetic eye exam. Their office will call you to schedule. If you have not heard from them in 10 days, call 404-555-0134.

items.title: Next clinic visit
items.plain_language: Come back to the clinic in 3 months. Come sooner if you need to.
items.why: To check on your blood sugar and blood pressure.
items.when: In 3 months, or sooner if needed
items.source_quote: Return to clinic in 3 months, or sooner if needed.
items.question_for_clinic: Can you help me book my 3-month visit now?

items.title: Check your blood sugar
items.plain_language: Check your blood sugar every morning before you eat breakfast. Write down the number. Bring your list to your next visit.
items.why: So you and your doctor can see your numbers.
items.source_quote: Check your blood sugar every morning before breakfast and write down the number. Bring your log to your next visit.
items.question_for_clinic: Do I need a blood sugar meter and supplies, and how do I get them?

items.title: Walk
items.plain_language: Walk for 30 minutes, 5 days a week, if you are able to.
items.why: The paper does not say why.
items.source_quote: Walk 30 minutes, 5 days a week, as tolerated.

items.title: Cut back on sugary drinks
items.plain_language: Drink less soda, sweet tea, and other sugary drinks.
items.why: The paper does not say why.
items.source_quote: Limit sugary drinks such as soda and sweet tea.

items.title: Very high blood sugar
items.plain_language: Call the office if your blood sugar is over 300 two times in a row.
items.why: This may mean you need help fast.
items.source_quote: Call the office if your blood sugar is above 300 two times in a row.
items.question_for_clinic: What phone number should I call, and what do I do if the office is closed?

items.title: Call 911 for these signs
items.plain_language: Call 911 or go to the emergency room if you have chest pain, trouble breathing, or sudden weakness on one side of your body.
items.why: These can be signs of an emergency.
items.source_quote: Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room if you have chest pain, trouble breathing, or sudden weakness on one side of your body.
